hotspot_verdict.decision: Patch is the larger hotspot but fails the strong same-bank baseline gate; bottleneck Conv is the selected performance line because it has the stronger fairer standalone cycle target.

patch_verdict.decision: Freeze patch as a negative/fairness ablation; do not spend the main Synopsys lane on patch performance RTL.

conv_verdict.selected_path: M152 bank-aware source-K4 -> fused M154 macro-output token -> row-interleaved no-forward Acc19 accumulator

paper_metric_structure.primary_incremental: 1.687017659x cycle-model target versus block-K4 with the same PWP1024 source port
paper_metric_structure.secondary_genealogy: 1.805357581x versus M143 B4/PWP512; explicitly bundles port widening
paper_metric_structure.secondary_dense: 14.858350695x versus fixed8 dense service opportunity; only after matched cycle-simulator baseline calibration
paper_metric_structure.forbidden: Do not promote any of the three to measured/RTL-calibrated speedup before the fused path, macro ports, and finite trace are closed.

selected_next_gate.name: fused_M154_source_major_no_forward_Acc19
vcs_requirements: Bind sequence/operator/window/partition/source/destination-half/row identity through the full producer-to-accumulator path.
Replay real signed INT8 checkpoint vectors and an exact ordered heldout trace subset.
Prove M152 modulo-four destination banking and row-interleaved no-forward II=1 against an M155 arithmetic miter.
Prove accepted exact-once coefficients under stalls, reset, stale tags, replay and cache alias before deleting the runtime overflow tree.
Preserve already accepted macro response/update state under every younger protocol fault.
dc_requirements: Synthesize the exact M155 forwarding baseline and fused no-forward candidate under one 3 ns TSMC28 flow.
Price deletion of M154's 3072-bit result register and M155's 7296-bit forwarding payload separately.
Keep the 3072-bit lazy-valid state and overflow guard in the first candidate; remove only after exact-once admission.
Bind four 32x768 INT8 weight SRAM cuts and four 768x96x19 accumulator SRAM port/timing contracts.
Report area, setup/hold, fanout and macro boundary; do not use the unsealed M155 debug point as paper PPA.
cycle_simulator_requirements: Use the 126581635-cycle block-K4/PWP1024 point as the primary same-port sparse parent.
Charge source-key/phase load, SRAM read latency, backpressure, accumulator write and final commit on the ordered trace.
Calibrate each latency/II with VCS and show a per-transaction miter on a bounded trace.
Report vector-read work separately from cycles and energy.

P0.title: Selected Conv path is not connected
P0.detail: M152 ordering, M154 vector supply and M155 accumulation have not been instantiated as one exact trace-driven module. M155 remains an unsealed debug anchor, and M158 independent review still blocks runtime overflow-tree deletion until accepted exact-once behavior is proved.

P0.title: Same-resource macro and finite-cycle baseline are absent
P0.detail: The 1.687x target has no selected SRAM macros, load-to-use recurrence, accumulator commit, energy or matched DC area. The 1.805x and 14.858x comparisons are broader baselines, not substitute evidence.

P1.title: Patch performance mainline fails its own fair gate
P1.detail: The best legal 8x128-bit point is only 1.1049x with 128 lanes versus the 96-lane K1 baseline; the M218-like point is slower.

P1.title: M149 is not integration-ready
P1.detail: Its stalled-result younger-fault counterexample remains, and the selected M152 route makes its conflict combine unnecessary for only a 0.00426% cycle penalty.

P1.title: M154 resident storage and load are external
P1.detail: The 98,304-bit weight store, checkpoint loading and physical macro-output hold semantics are excluded; its 3,072-bit result register is expensive but not yet legally deleted.

P1.title: M155 is the physical timing bottleneck
P1.detail: The zero-macro debug DC is 76,994.064 um2, 50 logic levels and +0.0164 ns setup slack; it contains 7,296 forwarding bits, 3,072 valid bits and a 384-lane overflow reduction cone.

P1.title: Cache reuse is not an incremental cycle result
P1.detail: 22.747x is uncached/cached vector read work, while M152 already charges the cached phase-load tokens.

P1.title: Row-interleave safety is frozen-trace-specific
P1.detail: Zero hazards hold for the checked heldout ordering, not arbitrary traffic; finite scheduling and fallback behavior remain required.

P1.title: Populations are not one end-to-end run
P1.detail: The full envelope ledger, patch s10 traces and bottleneck heldout20 recurrence have different populations; derived 1.027x, 1.055x and 1.085x figures are Amdahl sensitivities only.

P2.title: M36 is intrusive statistics-only evidence
P2.detail: Its nonbinary temporal counts cannot be turned into weighted Conv cycles.

P2.title: Patch empty-token skip needs a typed sparse consumer
P2.detail: Skipping all empty output commits is worth only 1.00387x even before encoding/ordering costs.

P2.title: PWP1024 is not an energy-saving claim
P2.detail: It cuts beats by 49.37% but transfers 1.263% more raw bits and doubles peak port bandwidth.

P2.title: Prediction Conv is immaterial
P2.detail: All four prediction Conv operators total only 271,156 cycles, 0.0437% of the frozen envelope.

allowed_claims: Conv2d accounts for 279,322,733 cycles (45.03%) of the frozen compute envelope; patch and bottleneck account for 32.15% and 12.84% respectively.
Under the current 8x128-bit patch contract, K4/D32 is the best legal point at 1.104921x, while K8/D16 is 0.946285x; wider 1.79x-4.45x points are resource expansion.
M152 is only 3,196 cycles (0.00426%) slower than M147 while avoiding the same-destination combine path.
The selected bottleneck Conv cycle-model target is 1.687018x versus a same-PWP1024 block-K4 parent; 1.805358x versus M143/PWP512 is a bundled genealogy comparison.
M157's 22.747x is vector-read work reduction and M155 is the next measured logic bottleneck, not an achieved speedup.
forbidden_claims: Do not claim achieved standalone Conv speedup, full-network speedup, throughput, energy or paper PPA.
Do not claim 1.805x as the primary same-resource incremental result or 14.858x as measured hardware speedup.
Do not claim M149 is integration-ready or part of the selected performance path.
Do not claim M154 output-register, M155 forwarding payload or overflow tree has already been removed.
Do not claim patch 1.79x-4.45x points under the 8-bank resource budget.
